author: Rahul kp
title: Lessee: Day One
simple_words: At commencement, the lessee books an asset for the right to use and a liability for the rent still to be paid.

definitions.meaning: Present value of lease payments not yet paid at the commencement date, discounted at the rate implicit in the lease, else the lessee's incremental borrowing rate.
Lessee's right to use the leased asset for the lease term. Measured at cost: lease liability plus certain other amounts.

key_points: Applies to the lessee's books under ==Ind AS 116==; one single lessee model, no finance/operating split
Short-term (12 months or less) and low-value leases: lessee may opt to expense payments straight-line
Variable payments linked to sales or usage are !!not included!! in the liability; they are expensed when incurred
Index- or rate-linked variable payments are included, using the index/rate at commencement

formulas.name: Lease liability at commencement
formulas.legend: P = lease payment unpaid at commencement; r = implicit rate (else IBR); t = period of payment

formulas.name: ROU asset at cost
formulas.legend: LL = lease liability; LP = payments made at/before start; D = initial direct costs; R = restoration estimate; I = incentives received

insight.punchline: Liability is the base, ROU adds extras!
insight.text: ROU equals the liability only when there are no prepayments, direct costs, restoration costs or incentives.

memory_trick.explanation: LL + LP + D + R − I. Everything is added except the incentive (Incentive is the one received, so it is minus).

exam_tip: Write the journal: Dr ROU asset, Cr Lease liability (and Cr Cash for payments made at start). Marks follow the working of both.

doubt.question: Do we use the IBR every time?
doubt.answer: No. Use the rate implicit in the lease if it can be readily determined. Only otherwise use the lessee's incremental borrowing rate.

mistakes.wrong: Including sales-linked variable rent in the lease liability
mistakes.right: Exclude it; recognise it in profit or loss when incurred. Include only index- or rate-linked variable payments.

mistakes.wrong: Adding lease incentives received to the ROU asset
mistakes.right: Lease incentives received reduce the ROU asset cost (they are deducted).

mistakes.wrong: Discounting at IBR even when the implicit rate is known
mistakes.right: Use the implicit rate if readily determinable; otherwise IBR.

mistakes.wrong: Ignoring the restoration cost when measuring the ROU asset
mistakes.right: Include the estimated restoration cost in ROU asset cost, as per Ind AS 37 obligation.

reviewer_note: Check that the paper tests Ind AS (assumed). Lease payments in the liability also include purchase option price if reasonably certain, residual value guarantees and termination penalties; omitted for space.
check_notes: Writer: Check that the paper tests Ind AS (assumed). Lease payments in the liability also include purchase option price if reasonably certain, residual value guarantees and termination penalties; omitted for space.

Checker 1: Definition 1 (Lease liability): the condition 'readily determinable' is missing. Correct version: 'discounted at the interest rate implicit in the lease if that rate can be readily determined; otherwise at the lessee's incremental borrowing rate.' The doubt answer and mistake 3 already say this; the definition should match them.

Checker 1: Formula 2 legend (R = restoration estimate): the restoration amount goes into the ROU asset as an estimate measured under Ind AS 37, which usually means its present value. Mistake 4 should say the same thing. Correct version: 'R = estimated cost of dismantling, removal or restoration, measured under Ind AS 37 (normally discounted to present value).'

Checker 1: Key point 2 (short-term and low-value leases): the short-term exemption needs two conditions: a lease term of 12 months or less AND no purchase option. The election is made by class of underlying asset for short-term leases, and lease by lease for low-value leases. Payments are expensed on a straight-line basis or another systematic basis.

Checker 1: Exam tip (journal): when there is a restoration obligation, the entry should also show 'Cr Provision for restoration (Ind AS 37)'. Initial direct costs paid should also be credited to Cash/Payables. Correct version: 'Dr ROU asset; Cr Lease liability; Cr Cash (prepaid payments and initial direct costs); Cr Provision for restoration; Dr Cash/Receivable for any incentives received.'

Checker 1: Memory trick ('Liability Plus Dad's Rent Incentive'): the word 'Rent' is used for R, but R stands for restoration cost. A student could think rent is added a second time. Use a word starting with 'Restore' instead, or state clearly in the explanation that R = restoration, not rent.

Checker 2: Memory trick 'Liability Plus Dad's Rent Incentive': the R in the formula stands for the restoration (dismantling) cost estimate, not rent. A student could read 'Rent' as rent payments, which are already in LL. Reword it, for example 'Liability Plus Dad's Restoration Incentive', or write 'R = Restoration' in the explanation. Also, 'Dad' for direct costs is fine, but 'LP' should be explained as prepaid or advance lease payments. This is wording only; the formula and signs are correct.
